x: Another who has performed well is Nicholas Head who joined us towards the end of the season. He has twice thrown the javelin within 2" of the Club record of 198'5".
Boosey set a meeting record with a winning triple jump of 49'9¾" and Head, a new member of great promise, threw the javelin 198'2" for a 4th place.
Nicholas Head and Barry King once again came 1st and 2nd in the Javelin,and good performances were also put up by John Thresher and Peter Hilliar in the 880y.

Both field events were won by Nicholas Head who looks as if he will be a valuable asset in the future. This is the first match we have won this year and shows what can be done when we turn out a full team.
One of the revelations was the casual ease with which Nick Head broke the Javelin record. From a run-up of a few yards he threw 207'7¾" - almost 20 feet further than Colin Clair's 1963 record.

Nick Head in his first competition of the season pushed up the club record for the Javelin to 203'3½".After the competition he threw even farther - so it looks as if some good things are in store from him this summer.

Nick Head once again broke the Club Record in winning the Javelin - this time an improvement of 7'0". In the 1500m Geoff North sliced a considerable chunk off his best mile time (conversion-wise that is) showing that he is out to give John Thresher a run for his money this season.

Senior Club Records were set by Nick Head (Jav), Geoff North (2m/3m) and equalled by Jim Vivian (100y). Junior Club Records were set by John Mitchell (L.Jump), Jim Vivian (100y), Bob Jones (Triple Jump) and by our relay squad in both sprint relays.

Nick Head turns out often and usually goes very close, if not over, 200 feet. However, Field Event Captain Brian King, who upped his best last year by 20 feet to 185 feet, added still more in his first competition of the season in spite of being troubled by a bruised throwing arm.

The conditions sadly affected our field event men with Nick Head being injured in the Javelin, our two Long Jumpers suffering from the anti-climax of their performances the previous week and Barry Townsend recovering from the SCAAA Decathlon held the day before.

The fine array of 21 trophies on view were largley hogged by Nick Head (Javelin, Weight, Discus), Jim Vivian (100,220,440), Tony Brooks (Jun 220, Jun 440) and Arnold Bent (Sen and Jun high jumps), but performances were not quite up to expectations.

To help the 80% of our readers who fail to understand our centre pages "satire" supplement(!) we reproduce the sort of advert which, with any luck, will one day embarrass those administrators who make those illogical decisions on amateur status. More power to your elbow NICK HEAD, and bad luck Ann Packer!

Our Field Event specialists were short of Nick Head, who had to go abroad at the last moment, and therefore several of our 'B' men had to move up into the 'A' events and we had to start looking around for second string men to fill their places.
Top points scorer of the day, though, was Nicholas Head with 3rd in the Javelin and 5th in the Shot and Discus, both the latter being close to his best ever.

However, the 'Field Boys' were already making up for the unexpected loss of points - Bill Couzens making the final six in the Hammer and Nicholas Head, in great shape, heaving the discus 123'11" for 4th place (a sandwich in his non-throwing hand)
The only other field event performance of any significance was Nick Head's winning throw in the Brockman Trophy. On the track there were more performances that rated high with the best in the land.

Throwers Nick Head, Brian King, Frank Glass and John Martin promise even even better performances next season. Our pole vaulters Barry Townsend and Denzil Winsborrow will certainly master the fibre glass pole and then (not wanting to be corny) "the sky's the limit".

… Mitchell and Alan Lerwill (2nd claim but completely Belgrave coached) in the long jump, and very close to them we have Nick Head (Javelin), Derek Wade (Long Jump), Brian King (Javelin), Frank Glass (Discus), Bob Couillault (Triple Jump), Denzil Winsborrow (Pole Vault and High Jump) and Barry Townse…
Nick Head and field events captain Brian King make this one of our strong events and the right day could have both men over 200 ft.
We had our share of victories, gaining first, second and third places in the high jump, a Nick Head win in the javelin(as usual) and Bob Couillault's double in the long and triple jumps.

The outstanding performers at this year's championships were Steve White, Chris Martin and Nick Head. The first two chalked up sprint trebles in the Junior & Senior grades respectively, and the latter repeated his "pinta" treble of last year shot/discus/javelin.
Nick Head did season's bests in Javelin and Shot, as did Tony Brooks in his heat of the 800 metres. Jim Vivian finished 5th in the 200 metres final and John Dear 4th in steeplechase (9:51.6).

With Nick Head out of the Country and Frank Glass unable to attend the first two meetings this exposed our shallowness in the Shot and Discus with our men only picking-up a consolation point in each event.
There were other good performances by Nick Head (Javelin and Discus), Bob Couillault (Triple), new member Robertson (Hammer), Tony Brooks (400) and Peter Hilliar (800).
Otherwise Nick Head and Frank Glass shared the throwing events between them,with a particularly close javelin competition going to Nick ahead of Brian King.
Nick Head (Javelin, Shot) In Germany during 2 meetings. With these men in the team we would certainly have avoided relegation, but what of our cert promotion prospects into the Second division?
Nick Head is back in the country again and is already finding form with the Javelin, with Steve Inman close on his heels. This partnership has already given us maximum points in the Malkin Trophy.
